newsitem.title: USA: Heat kills California child left inside truck.
newsitem.headline: Heat kills California child left inside truck.

text.p: A 13-month-old girl died after being left in a truck for eight hours by her father in searing temperatures of up to 150 degrees Fahrenheit (65.55 Celsius) after he went to work and forgot about her, police said on Friday.

Darren Rodrigues, 29, strapped his daughter Brianna in a child seat in his Ford Explorer when he left his home in Turlock, 100 miles (160 km) southeast of San Francisco, on Wednesday morning to go to work, police spokesman Bob Nicholas said.
Rodrigues was meant to drop off the child at a day care centre but forgot and drove straight to his office. He parked the vehicle, forgetting the child was still in the back seat.

Rodrigues worked all day and did not remember his daughter until 5 P.M. when his wife Nicole, 24, called him from the day care centre where she had gone to pick up the child after leaving her job, Nicholas said.
"She asked the father where the child was. It hit the father he had forgotten to drop the child off," Nicholas said.
Rodrigues ran to the vehicle and took the child out. Paramedics and police were called but "the child had already passed away due to the heat," Nicholas said.
He estimated that temperatures inside the vehicle had reached between 130 (54.5C) and 150 degrees Fahrenheit.
"It's a mind-boggler. Everybody's going: How can that happen?" Nicholas said.
He said detectives had concluded the father "simply forgot" about the child.

Rodrigues was deeply upset after the incident. "He appeared to be in some state of shock," Nicholas said. He said the father or mother usually dropped off their daughter at the day care centre depending on their schedules.
Nicholas said police were compiling reports and awaiting results of the autopsy, expected within two weeks.
The police department would then give the information to the local District Attorney to decide whether to file charges. Nicholas would not speculate whether charges could be filed.
